To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients dying of heart disease received less adequate end-of-life care than those with cancer, despite being similar in age, gender and place of death.
patients dying of cancer compared to those dying of heart disease had more shortness-of-breath, fewer drugs prescribed for symptom relief and more often died in a healthcare setting.
patients with heart disease were less likely than those with cancer to receive the recommended care during the last days of life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of care for patients with heart failure and cancer in their last week of life.
how patients with heart disease are cared for in the last weeks of their lives.
how the care for the dying in Sweden can be improved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are significant differences in the quality of end-of-life care in the last week of dying patients’ life in Sweden.
the end-of-life care provided to dying heart disease patients is unequal to that of cancer patients.
patients dying from heart disease received less care than patients dying of cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a need to change the culture of palliative care in order to provide equal end-of-life care for patients with heart diseases.
the patients dying from heart diseases are not as well prepared for their death as the patients dying from cancer.
there is a need to develop a new model of end-of-life care for heart disease patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the care for heart disease patients is less good than the care for cancer patients.
the quality of care for patients with heart failure and other non-cancer diagnoses is not satisfactory and needs to be addressed in future research and in clinical practice.
there is a need for new and more effective models of end-of-life care that can be implemented in all care settings and for all patients regardless of diagnosis.
